operations.name: Suggest options from a website
operations.agentTask: Read the website in `sourceUrl` and write three different ways to fill the ad "Result seen through the product". Objective: Tie an impressive output directly to the product that creates it. Visual rule: The result and the product window align spatially; a mask explains the relationship. Beats, in order: - 0–2 s: The impressive output fills the scene. Shows Brand color, Result image, Result line. - 2–4.5 s: Product/window frame appears over the aligned result. Shows Brand color, Result image, Product frame, Product line. - 4.5–7.5 s: Window content shows a relevant change or detail. Shows Brand color, Result image, Product frame, Feature line. - 7.5–9.5 s: Pull back to an intelligible product-plus-result composition. Shows Brand color, Result image, Product frame, Benefit. - 9.5–12 s: Result, product and next step remain visible. Shows Brand color, Result image, Product frame, Logo, Call to action. Use only facts the website or pages you read state. Never invent prices, discounts, dates, guarantees or claims. When a fact a field needs is missing, write a short placeholder in square brackets, such as [offer end date]. Make the three options clearly different in angle, wording and image choice. For images, choose real, large images of this brand and product: first from the page's own images (header logo, large files, feature-page screenshots), then with an image search. A social preview card (og:image, a title on a gradient) is a last resort. Give the direct URL of the image file, never a page URL, and never an image of another brand. Use an empty string when no image fits. If image search throws because no search backend is configured, tell the user in one sentence that a SerpAPI, DataForSEO or Brave key in Settings finds better images. Then take nodetool.web.screenshot of the product's feature pages instead. Save each image you consider as an asset and look at it with view_image before you offer it. Name in the option's description any image that is only a social preview card. Write `fillOptions` as a list of three objects, `fillChoice` as "" and `fillReport` as "". Each option: - value: "1", "2" or "3" - title: a name for the direction in 2 to 4 words - description: one sentence on what it emphasizes, then the first two copy lines in quotes - image: the URL of its first image, for the option card - brandColor: the brand's accent color as #RRGGBB (buttons, links, highlights), not the page background or a theme-color that is near black or white - fields: resultLabel (Result line: result hook, at most 7 words); productLink (Product line: frame reveal, at most 7 words); featureAction (Feature line: demonstrate, at most 7 words); benefit (Benefit: benefit, at most 7 words); cta (Call to action: cta, at most 4 words) - images: resultImage (Result image: A real photo or screenshot that matches the beats that show it. Shown in: The impressive output fills the scene. | Product/window frame appears over the aligned result. | Window content shows a relevant change or detail. | Pull back to an intelligible product-plus-result composition. | Result, product and next step remain visible.); productFrame (Product frame: A shot of the product alone, ideally on a plain or transparent background, so it reads as a cutout. Shown in: Product/window frame appears over the aligned result. | Window content shows a relevant change or detail. | Pull back to an intelligible product-plus-result composition. | Result, product and next step remain visible.); logo (Logo: The brand's own logo file, such as the site header logo or its icon. Shown in: Result, product and next step remain visible.) Then show the Start step with `only: ["fillChoice"]` and a one-sentence note, so the user sees just the option cards. Picking one runs `apply`, which saves the images and fills the steps.
